items.title: Google shipped Gemini scam text screening
items.oneliner: Google is putting Gemini into Android Messages for scam detection, which makes on-device trust and false positives product-critical.

items.title: Krea pushed image editing speed down
items.oneliner: Krea 3 claims 4x faster image editing at $0.135 per image, pushing creative tooling toward real-time iteration.

items.title: Interpretability got a serious counterargument
items.oneliner: Goodfire argues neural nets are cleaner than we thought, which could reset how teams approach mechanistic interpretability.

items.title: Targeted ads became a spyware pipeline
items.oneliner: Citizen Lab found zero-click spyware delivered through targeted ads across nearly 200,000 sites and apps.

items.title: HTTP headers became an injection surface
items.oneliner: A scan of 217 million responses found AI-targeted headers on 7,959 sites, including prompt injection attempts.

items.title: States sued OpenAI over child safety
items.oneliner: Eight states sued OpenAI over alleged harms to children, raising real product liability pressure for consumer AI.

items.title: ASML warned chip demand will outrun supply
items.oneliner: ASML says AI chip demand may exceed its 2027 and 2028 plans, so compute scarcity is still the default assumption.

items.title: Libreboot added broad UEFI support
items.oneliner: Libreboot 26.10 switched to EDK2 and added 233 Chromebook models, making open firmware less niche overnight.

items.title: OpenCode moved to a background server
items.oneliner: OpenCode 2.0 adopted a client-server architecture with plugin hot reload, which makes automation and scheduled workflows much easier.

items.title: UTC changes are becoming an engineering problem
items.oneliner: Standards bodies are preparing UTC changes by 2035, and every distributed system team should treat time as fragile infrastructure.
